Hi, [~accountid:60e708db7f191f0069879290]! Apologies for the delay. I have reviewed the comments made by Thai Wok and below you will find my responses. Please kindly translate the questions of the partners that you require help with in the future to speed up the process. 

# Definition of Courier - Bolt is not providing delivery services and does not employ couriers. Couriers act as independent contractors. Therefore, Bolt does not assume liability for the actions of couriers and we are not able to agree to the proposed change.
# Clause 2 - Unfortunately, I was not able to understand what partner tried to say. Can you please clarify with them? I refer to this comment "Proszę wpisać w umowę na wszelkie wypadek, że konstytuuje ona wyłączności Bolt".
# Clause 2.3 - We cannot accept the suggestion to have joint and several liability due to the reasons mentioned in point 1.
# Clause 5.5 - The effective functioning of the Bolt Food Platform in not only dependent on Bolt, but also on a lot of other service providers (e.g. server providers), and therefore, we are not able to accept any amendment requests. However, this we are able to consider a compromise for key players. Is this partner a key restaurant? We are definitely not able to accept deletion of the last sentence as we cannot bear damages that result from the partner's non-compliance.
# Clause 6.2 - For some reason the clause in the T&Cs version that the partner commented is not the same as in our up to date T&Cs available[ here|https://static.food.bolt.eu/legalDocument/491PwFrS6ux4UMtTK3x6HE/V5%20of%20Bolt-Partner%20General%20Terms%20(PL)%20-ENG_PL-%20-clean-.pdf] and this caused the problem because the clause that the partner commented missed very important bit. You can always get the most up to date General T&Cs from this [page|https://food.bolt.eu/legal]. Here we talk only about Marketplace Fees that will not exceed the Agency Fee and should not cause any worry to the partner.
# Clause 7.4 - this can be added to the Special Terms if needed. The suggested wording is requiring business decision, but legally there is no problem. The acceptable wording is mentioned in this [contracting playbook|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2425522072/Partners] for clause 7.8.
# Clause 7.8 - I strongly recommend not to accept deletion of the last 2 sentences. Whether or not to accept changes related to the interest rate is a business decision.
# Clause 8.2 - We cannot accept the proposed change as Bolt needs to protect itself and in some cases immediate suspension is required. Bolt is interested in partner's successful usage of Bolt Food Platform and no suspension will be triggered unless it is absolutely necessary.
# Clause 8.4 - not sure what is the benefit for the partner to add this provisions, but we can add it to the Special Terms.
# Clause 12.2 - we cannot agree to accept liability for loss of profit.
# Clause 12.3 - we prefer to leave this clause unchanged, but what they are asking for is actually more beneficial to us rather than to them. Let's try to push back, but if they don't agree, we can figure something out.
# Clause 12.4 - this is our standard clause, please push back.
# Clause 12.5 - same as clause 12.4.
# Clause 12.10 - same as clause 12.4.
# Clause 13.4 - we can agree to this, but this needs to be reflected in the Special Terms.
# Clause 13.5 - We will notify the partner 30 days in advance and the partner can terminate the agreement by giving 30 days' prior written notice. The risk for the partner is reduced due to the notification period regarding changes. Therefore, please push back.
# Clause 13.7 - we can agree to their suggestion with slight change - the court would be one of courts in Poland, but just a common court.

*Next steps:*

# Please kindly communicate our response to the partner and also share the most up to date version of the [General T&Cs|https://static.food.bolt.eu/legalDocument/491PwFrS6ux4UMtTK3x6HE/V5%20of%20Bolt-Partner%20General%20Terms%20(PL)%20-ENG_PL-%20-clean-.pdf] with them. 
# Please prepare Special Terms that will reflect the necessary agreed changes. You can find the template of Special Terms [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2577203498/Bolt+Food+Terms+Conditions+and+Templates]. Police returned;

Some of the information is classified, which makes it difficult for me to disclose.

If you follow the situation in the Stockholm region since August 2023, the violence has escalated enormously. There are several groups that fight each other and many innocent people become victims of these crimes. We want to prevent that.

The crimes in question include: Completed murder, attempted murder, arson and several serious weapons offences.

Regarding the law, please see below:

"Request to access data with the support of 6.1 f of the data protection regulation.

According to 6.1 f of the data protection regulation, processing is only legal if and to the extent that the processing i.a. is necessary for purposes related to the legitimate interests of the data controller or a third party, unless the data subject's interests or fundamental rights and freedoms outweigh and require the protection of personal data.

A preliminary investigation has been started in the matter according to ch. 23. Section 1 of the Code of Procedure. The preliminary investigation concerns a serious crime for which, according to the BrB, no lighter punishment than imprisonment of more than two years is prescribed for the crime.

According to ch. 23 § 2 of the Code of Procedure, the Police Authority must collect evidence during a preliminary investigation to investigate who can reasonably be suspected of a crime and whether there are sufficient grounds for prosecution.

The police authority may collect and process personal data in order to investigate and prosecute crimes according to ch. 2. 1 § 2 of the Act (2018:1693) on the police's processing of personal data within the scope of the Criminal Data Act.

According to ch. 1, the police authority is Section 4 of the Act on the police's processing of personal data within the area of the Criminal Data Act personal data controller for the processing of personal data carried out by the authority.

# Purpose limitation - we must clearly state the intended purposes of the call recording
# Security - ensure that the data is stored securely
# Data subject rights - we must ensure that data is easily accessible and retrievable when needed.
# Devices - we must identify all the recording devices used and all types of recordings stored;
# Record-keeping - we must ensure that recordings are created, managed, and disposed of in accordance with record-keeping requirements and business needs;

 We have already established that GDPR does not apply.  Here are some useful points to consider, given the estate rules seem to be similar to ones in England & Wales:



# *Please if you could advise whether there are any laws/rules in Sweden that can regulate provision/disclosure of data of a deceased person?*

No, GDPR applies and there are no special provisions under Swedish law providing for protection of personal data of a deceased person.

*_2. Would it be the equivalent of e.g. an estate in England that would be authorised to make such a request?_*

General about Swedish estates:

* When a person dies, the assets and liabilities pass to their estate. The estate is a legal entity that can itself have rights and obligations. The estate is represented by the surviving cohabitant or spouse, where such exists, and the deceased's heirs according to law and/or due to a will (may include close family members). In some cases, the heirs of a previously deceased spouse can also be joint owners of the deceased's estate. All co-owners of the estate jointly represent the estate in all matters.
* When a person dies, a probate must be drawn up showing who or who are the deceased's estate owners as well as the deceased's assets and liabilities.
* The estate record must be registered with the Tax Agency and, once it has been registered, it is a document of authority that the representative of the estate must show when, for example, carrying out business at the bank.
* If the deceased was a foreign citizen or alternatively resided abroad, other rules may apply.

*3. Would the request need to be made via a different/official channel rather than by an alleged family member?*

It depends on whether the estate is represented by the family member making the request. A Swedish estate can be represented by:

* The estate co-owners jointly, who prove their right to represent the estate through a registered estate register
* Estate attorney appointed by the district court
* Executor appointed by the deceased in his will after it became legally binding

Hello [~accountid:61d43127bce5e000692f2632] ,

In response to your question:

*_-”What could we state in Special terms so the Partner would be calm that we care all liability regarding checking the IDs and not giving away the orders if the customer doesn't have minimal age for drinking?-”_*

Short answer: No, we can't and we have to stick with what was stated in the General Terms… Below I share with you the reasons why:

* Firstly, we have to differentiate the role of the partner and the role of Bolt in this sale agreement:
** Bolt offers Platform services while the Partner is the seller who holds the license to sell alcohol.
** In this case, the contractual relation in the Platform are as follows: sales agreement for the sale of goods between the restaurant/store and the consumer.
* The requirements for the sale of alcohol set out in the Law, must be complied by the Retailer as he is the License holder. In this sense, although the sale is performed via Bolt App, the Partner should ensure that the whole process is compliant with all regulations and legal requirements at its own risk.

This is the understanding and the main reasons why Bolt cannot assume responsibility for regulatory compliance with respect to the age of majority, among others.

On the other hand, I totally get your point that the Partner is, at some point, relying on our couriers and eventually held responsible for something that is not entirely under his direct control.

I know that the consumer is consulted and must state his/her legal age through the app while placing an alcoholic order. However, the correct way to go should be asking for the ID to prove age before handing in the drinks, I also know that couriers are being educated on this point and the app should have a way of verifying age as well.

For more insight info about age verifications and how we are contributing with Partners to ensure compliance on this point, please take a look to the channel #feature-eater-age-check .

I hope that this overview responds to your question, if not, please let me know and I’m happy to explain further... I’ll be attentive to your comments.

PS: We don’t have minor age couriers so there should be no concerns on this point.

*_My order price was Miscalculated - UPDATE_*

*PR Context - Findings based on the deep-dive*

* P_rice is wrong_ reason is very broad and better granularity could help us to solve the general complaints by automation.
* When drivers believe they were undercharged they. can submit Price Reviews with _the price is wrong reason._ Such cases are closed to an upfront price as the price hasn’t *exceeded the upper recalculation threshold*. [Example|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/467783968/717777263], [Example 2|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/467519519/716619913]
* [The upfront threshold (%) |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013391799]indicates how much the accurate price needs to differ from the _Upfront_ in order to justify manually adjusting the price. However, this is being calculated in the background therefore no manual recalculation with the Price Review tool is not needed.

*CS Volumes Context - Findings based on the deep-dive*
If Rider is being overcharged due to upfront price [thresholds|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/pricing-config/pricing-config-beta?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22status%22%3Atrue%2C%22country%22%3A%22ee%22%2C%22cityIds%22%3A%5B1%5D%7D%7D], we tell them that the price is not set in stone. If the driver is unhappy that the price didn’t change, we are not referring to the thresholds but to the estimated price logic. However, the automation containing the pricing logic won’t send the ticket volumes away.
The current automation reply[ is this one |https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CD/pages/4445636144/Driver+Low+Fares]but that contains only complaints about the tariffs and is not educating the driver on "this price is correct because of XY". We need to have a technical solution once the driver shares the final price complaint and be clear in communication to avoid situations as visible in the screenshot attached.

Sample: 40 tickets

*Volume Findings:*

PR not raised 73%

PR was raised and the price was changed *0%*



*PEX Scope - Summary*

* The analysis makes it clear that Price Reviews don't really benefit the drivers. In our playbooks, we guide agents to manually adjust prices and encourage drivers to share any pricing concerns with us directly while it brings no to little value.
* If we can quickly tweak the price or drop it to zero with a simple review change, that's great. But let's not go for it if it means CS has to make manual changes.
* In our processes, we’re advising the agents to manually recalculate the price for cases when thresholds are not exceeded.  As visible in the deep-dive, this approach will only lead to closing the price to estimate, but we’re losing a lot of time with this approach.
* There are tickets in the analysis where we spend tens of minutes with back-and-forth convos with the drivers, repeating that the price is correct and we haven’t found any irregularities. The agent handling it will do nothing - assuming the price was calculated correctly, and the driver will get zero feedback. Consequently, this is negatively impacting our HT.
* Reducing friction for drivers with pricing issues, and taking their feedback more seriously will reduce driver churn. In order to improve this, we need to show real actions behind the price revisions

*My Feedback to Supportability - Summary*

* Price Reviews and CS tickets are duplicating the CS workload, with minimal benefit (no feedback to drivers, no feedback to pricing analyst team)
* The drivers often think the price was messed up when it's just following our pricing setup and recalculation benchmarks—unless we're talking about missing *toll fees*, *parking fees*, or *GPS issues* that caused the price drop. These are the only examples where a human touch is needed, as the price review can be closed to the correct price due to network issues or issues with the map. For general complaints, there is no point in having Price Reviews. By showing this option to the Drivers, we’re giving them mixed signals and wrong ideas about our pricing system, as we are not openly exposing our threshold recalculation logic.
* As seen above, more than 30% of the tickets in the sample were based on a frustration with market-specific pricing setup more than on specific technical issues that would lead to price miscalculation. In conclusion, the root cause of the low CSAT is general complaints about tariffs and price recalculation thresholds, both outside of the PEX scope
* From a Product perspective, [this|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02CUF8CFCZ/p1699892289279509] is a good example of how it could potentially look like when drivers are requesting random price reviews or raising the _Price is wrong_-related tickets.

*Update from Supportability - Mariia*

Ideally, next year, the flow will be more organized, following the structure mentioned [HERE|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CD/pages/4340384632/Driver+pricing+problems+and+feedback] (*this is a very good analysis for a better understanding of the overall root cause of those tickets*). It won't be an automation per se, but it should reduce the load on drivers when it comes to how they should/shouldn’t complain about such orders. A portion of this process will be automated.

*Update from Supportability - Sami*

We had a meeting with Tushar on 15/11, and I'm working with the PR topics more closely now, so will respond to your message with a slight delay. Next update after our meeting: 22/11





*Overall Summary:*

* Price is wrong reviews are always closed to the estimate with no changes, leading to driver friction and wasted time for the CS
* The process advises the agents to manually recalculate the price, which adds no value
* The agents are encouraging the drivers to submit price reviews whenever they have doubts about the price, which only leads to frustration, as CS cannot address or fix the general pricing complaints.



*Next steps:*

* Submit this analysis to Sami

konstantin.kulikov: The problem was related to our push to support full JSON specification for all post-requests across the micromobility domain.
As result, we wrapped body fields in the multipart post request in JSON format as well. The part looks like:
```--a72ac9d5-e00c-4134-bf56-444e6fcda799
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="validation_type"
Content-Length: 16
  
"mandatory_zone"```
You can see that the body part value is string and as a string in the root of a json structure, it wrapped in quotes.
But it turned out that on the backend side, it is not possible to handle json object inside a post request part. Instead, it just parses the part body as a string and grabs all parts together in one body. On the backend it looks like that:
```  "body": {
    "allow_finish_order_on_attempt": 2,
    "city_id": 32,
    "order_id": 105681523,
    "validation_type": "\"pavement_validation\""
  }```
You can see the json-represented string `mandatory_zone` was handled like just a string and quotes (that's a part of json syntax) were just included in the string value.

After discussing with @nikita.isakov, we agreed not to support a full-json format for multipart body and consider each par as a raw primitive value, not a json formatted string.

Mobile fix is here: https://github.com/bolteu/android-app-client/pull/10772
Will be included in release `CA.95.0`

shall first be submitted to the President of the Chamber, who shall decide on it in civil and commercial cases if he considers that it should be upheld in full. # Pursuant to the provisions of Section 374(3) of Act No 99/1963 Coll., the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended (hereinafter referred to as the Code of Civil Procedure), if an appeal is lodged against a decision issued by a judicial commissioner, a judicial officer, an assistant judge or an authorized administrative employee, the President of the Chamber (single judge) may grant the appeal in full. [~accountid:61addb80b0b630006a695081] from the recent Walless memo of 13th October 2023: 

* The Law on Alcohol Control *prohibits any advertisement* of alcoholic beverages. Any dissemination of information about beverages that may lead to their purchase is considered to be prohibited advertising, e.g. sales campaigns, display of individual shelves, additional/brighter lighting and therefore are not possible.
* The Law on Alcohol Control *prohibits the announcement of price reductions* for alcoholic beverages. *Displaying the price of the alcoholic beverage is considered an advertisement*, and *displaying prices is allowed only at a retail outlet or catering establishments where alcoholic beverages are sold to the consumer or on the websites of undertakings manufacturing or selling alcoholic beverages* (the Law on Alcohol Control article 29(2)). Based on this exception, the prices of alcoholic beverages may be available only on the websites / apps of the specific Retailers (licence holders). If not, prices, images of bottles and other information on specific alcoholic beverages may be considered illegal advertisement. The display of discounted prices and inclusion of alcoholic beverages into various promotions is also considered advertising and is prohibited. The price of the drink may be reduced, but the price label cannot show the reduction and only the single lower price may be displayed.
* In recent years, the change in the Law on Alcohol Control has not been supported by members of Parliament. This system could change if more liberal government is elected, the next parliamentary elections in LT will be in 2024. It is unrealistic to expect any change before these elections.
* The guidance on alcohol advertising produced by the consumer protection authorities is here: [https://ntakd.lrv.lt/uploads/ntakd/documents/files/Rekomendacijos_2021-01 NEW.pdf|https://ntakd.lrv.lt/uploads/ntakd/documents/files/Rekomendacijos_2021-01%20NEW.pdf]

h3. User cannot reserve a vehicle or order a trip due to negative Bolt Balance

If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:

*Step 1: Confirm charge details*

* Open User Balance > [Transaction history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
* Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
* Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
* Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date

*Step 2: Verify the cause*

* Open the Fraud > Calculations > [User page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
* Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
* Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.


IF you have any questions, please let me know.

As they would like to see addresses of the trips to identify possible *illegal use of the account*, this can include data about a third party who made these trips and the GDPR applies. We do have a right to disclose this in case of a fraud, but as we don’t have any proof of the family ties with the deceased person, it will be significantly difficult to justify the disclosure.

*I propose the following:*
1) ask the person who requested this data to confirm the date of the death or at least month, so we can check whether any trips were made after this data

2) If the trips were made, we can ask them to refer to police to investigate this case.

3) If they do not want to go to police, we have to have a proof of their family relationship to disclose this data  as per the privacy law we can disclose data about a third party if there is a fraud and this info can help the legitimate user of the account. But as the legitimate user of the account is deceased, we can provide this data to family members. 

* The issue here is that any birth certificate or marriage certificate will not work as we don’t verify names or other details of users except phone and email, but it’s not 100% proof. So in that case we recommend them going to police and we will be able to disclose this data to police.

Data Protection Act ([https://www.mdes.go.th/law/detail/1905-Personal-Data-Protection-Act--B-E--2562--2019-|https://www.mdes.go.th/law/detail/1905-Personal-Data-Protection-Act--B-E--2562--2019-])

*Section 41 The Data Controller and the Data Processor shall designate a data protection officer in the following circumstances:*
(1) the Data Controller or the Data Processor is a public authority as prescribed and announced by the Committee;
(2) the activities of the Data Controller or the Data Processor in the collection, use, or disclosure of the Personal Data require a regular monitoring of the Personal Data or the system, by the reason of having a large number of Personal Data as prescribed and announced by the Committee;
(3) the core activity of the Data Controller or the Data Processor is the collection, use, or disclosure of the Personal Data according to section 26.
In the event that the Data Controller or the Data Processor are in the same affiliated business or are in the same group of undertakings, in order to jointly operate the business or group of undertakings as prescribed and announced by the Committee according to section 29 paragraph two, such Data Controller or Data Processor may jointly designate a data protection officer. In this regard, each establishment of the Data Controller or the Data Processor in the same affiliated business or in the same group of undertakings must be able to easily contact the data protection officer.
The provisions in paragraph two shall apply to the Data Controller or the Data Processor who is a public authority in (1) that is large in size or has several establishments mutatis mutandis.
IntheeventthattheDataControllerortheDataProcessorin paragraphone has to designate the representative according to section 37 (5), the provisions in paragraph one shall apply to the representative mutatis mutandis.
The Data Controller and the Data Processor shall have an obligation to provide the information of the data protection officer, contact address, and contact channels to the data subject and the Office. The data subject shall be able to contact the data protection officer with respect to the collection, use, or disclosure of the Personal Data and the exercise of rights of the data subject under this Act.
The Committee may prescribe and announce the qualifications of the data protection officer by taking into account the knowledge or expertise with respect to the Personal Data protection.
The personal data protection officer may be a staff of the Data Controller or the Data Processor, or a service provider under the contract with the Data Controller or the Data Processor.

*Section 42 The data protection officer shall have the following duties:*
(1) give advices to the Data Controller or the Data Processor, including the employees or service providers of the Data Controller or of the Data Processor with respect to compliance with this Act;
(2) investigate the performance of the Data Controller or the Data Processor, including the employees or service providers of the Data Controller or of the Data Processor with respect to the collection, use, or disclosure of the Personal Data for compliance with this Act;
(3) coordinate and cooperate with the Office in the circumstance where there are problems with respect to the collection, use, or disclosure of the Personal Data undertaken by the Data Controller or the Data Processor, including the employees or service providers of the Data Controller or of the Data Processor with respect to the compliance with this Act;
(4) keep confidentiality of the Personal Data known or acquired in the course of his or her performance of duty under this Act.
The Data Controller or the Data Processor shall support the data protection officer in performing the tasks by providing adequate tools or equipment as well as facilitate the access to the Personal Data in order to perform the duties.
The Data Controller or the Data Processor shall not dismiss or terminate the data protection officer’s employment by the reason that the data protection officer performs his or her duties under this Act. In the event that there is any problem when performing the duties, the data protection officer must be able to directly report to the chief executive of the Data Controller or the Data Processor.
The data protection officer may be able to perform other duties or tasks but the Data Controller or the Data Processor must warrant to the Office that such duties or tasks are not against or contrary to the performance of the duties under this Act.

The Notification of the Personal Data Protection Committee re: Designation of a Data Protection Officer under Section 41 (2) of the Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019) B.E. 2566 (2023) ("*PDPC Notification re: DPO Designation*") has been published in the Government Gazette on 14 September 2023. This notification will be effective *from 13 December 2023.Criteria to designate a DPO*
Under the PDPC Notification re: DPO Designation, to determine whether to designate a DPO, the data controller or data processor must consider the following step-by-step criteria:*Step 1: Core activities criteria*
The PDPC Notification re: DPO Designation defines "core activities" as any operation that is necessary and significant to achieve the primary objectives or goals of the businesses. The definition also specifies samples of core activities. However, ancillary activities, which are activities that merely support the operation of the businesses, are not considered core activities.
*Step 2: Regular monitoring criteria*
The core activities would be considered as requiring regular monitoring of the personal data or system if they involve regular tracking, monitoring, analyzing, and profiling of personal data in a systematic way. The PDPC Notification re: DPO Designation also provides samples of activities, e.g., membership cards and electronic cards, credit scoring and fraud prevention, insurance premium consideration, behavioral advertising, computer networking services or telecommunications businesses, and surveillance and security services.
*Step 3: Large-scale criteria*
Various factors must be taken into account in order to consider if the core activities involve personal data on a large scale. One of the factors is whether the number of data subjects reaches 100,000 or more. However, there has not yet been any clarification on what type of data subjects would be counted as 100,000 data subjects for each company, e.g., whether corporate client's business contacts would be counted with end customers or not. Additionally, activities such as behavioral advertising through widely used search engines or social media, normal operations of insurance companies and financial institutions, and telecommunications businesses, also trigger large-scale criteria.

-----
the PDPC Notification re: *DPO Designation is still silent on the forms and qualifications of the DPO.* As such, the data controller or data processor would still have some level of flexibility in designating the DPO. However, the PDPC may issue another sub-regulation prescribing the DPO qualifications at a later stage.
Businesses under the PDPA should consider if they meet any of the criteria to designate a DPO. If so, they must complete the designation process and notify the information of the DPO to the data subjects and the Office of the PDPC by 13 December 2023.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Hello Thomas Ringen,

Thank you for your request which was received by us on November 2, 2023.

We provide you with the following information in relation to your request.

*Consent to receive notifications about app updates:* Our Privacy Policy for riders and passengers, specifically outlined in Section 8 (available at [https://bolt.eu/en-no/privacy/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-no/privacy/?category=rides]), details that in addition to obtaining your consent, we may also use a "soft opt-in" basis for legitimate interest in direct marketing. It is important to highlight that the GDPR explicitly acknowledges in Recital 47 that "the processing of personal data for direct marketing purposes may be regarded as carried out for a legitimate interest."

However, you have rightfully noted that generally opt-in consent is needed to send direct marketing communications - this is stipulated by Article 13(1) of the ePrivacy Directive. Yet, there are exceptions to this rule outlined in Article 13(2) of the same Directive. Specifically, this provision permits sending electronic direct marketing communications to existing customers without explicit opt-in consent, provided their contact details were obtained during a sale of a product or service. Since you are an active user of Bolt application and your contact details were acquired in this context, this exception is applicable in your case.

Please also note that where opt-in consent is required, such as receiving our partner offers that might interest you, you will not be opted in by default - and we will ask your opt in consent in this and all cases where required by law.

*Consent for location data collection:* Our app is designed not to request location access when it's closed. Our app provides three options to you when requesting access to location data "Allow Once", "Allow While Using App," or “Don’t Allow”. They do not permit location access when the app is not in use.

It's worth mentioning that users can manually grant background location access by selecting "Always" in the phone's Settings app for our application. However, it's crucial to clarify that we do not utilize location data in the background even if the user grants this permission. For the proper functioning of the app, "While Using the App" is the sufficient setting.

*Location data while app is not in use:* Apple enables apps to automatically trigger notifications when the user enters a specific geographical area. This does not require the app to run in background and mobile data to be used. Apple stores this information and automatically triggers those notifications without sharing the user’s location with Bolt. You can read more about the functionality directly on Apple’s website [here|https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/unlocationnotificationtrigger].

If this bothers you, you can disable this feature by going to _“My Profile - Communication Preferences - Travelling”_ and disable _“Travel Notifications”._ Disabling it will not affect your experience with Bolt.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.


Sincerely,
Bolt.

tl;dr: I would propose to implement a pipeline restart with the same parameters, but without keeping the locks. Keeping the locks sounds like solving the symptoms and not the core issues.

There are two main scenarios: releasing to PRELIVE-only and releasing to LIVE.

h3. Releasing to LIVE

For LIVE, allowing to keep locks for the pipeline sounds really dangerous. This will make it possible to try to release early when the feature is half-done and keep fixing the issues on the fly. This will make the lock contention even worse and it also would promote a dangerous pattern to release the feature earlier than it’s safe to do so.

What are the symptoms this solution might be trying to solve:

* High lock contention – this is a problem that won’t disappear on its own, it’s been there since the very beginning. In short, splitting services and packages to be more granular should help. If it’s about file locks, then those should be reviewed and we should take some similar action respectively. If some of those files are generated or some really common ones, then PINT should do something about those. Here’s an example of such action: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-750|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-750|smart-link] 
* Extra issues detected by checks in the pipeline that weren’t detected in the brach’s CI. I’d say here we’re trying our best to provide feedback as early as possible, to minimize the amount of such cases:
** There are some of the checks which can only be done during the build step, for example, checking if secrets were actually provided (due to the access restrictions). If we perform checks like this, we try to put them as early as possible into the pipeline, so that you would get the feedback ASAP. Moreover, we try to put them even before you acquire the locks, so that you wouldn’t have to wait in the queue only to find out that something was missing from your PR.
** Some of the checks could indeed be done before the pipeline is created, however they might be too expensive to run for all feature branches. This is why there are slight differences between CI checks in release branches and in feature branches. We try to keep those to minimum to make sure that it’s a rare case that a release branch CI fails, even though the feature branch CI passed.

h3. Releasing to PRELIVE

For PRELIVE, it’s a bit more reasonable if you’re trying to experiment with some service. However, it’s a symptom of another feature missing – some way of “developing services in PRELIVE”. We have discussed this internally and one of the ideas was to implement another version of “locrem” which would work similar to Admin Panel development. You would be able to develop some of the services locally, while the rest would be proxied to prelive, so you would be basically developing against prelive. This is still on the idea level, however it sounds like it could be a better solution rather than keeping locks in prelive.

h3. How much can you optimize by not restarting a pipeline?

The thing is, whenever you make any code change, you actually have to rerun most (if not all) of the steps in the pipeline. If locks are not an issue, then starting a pipeline from scratch with the same set of parameters shouldn’t be very different from keeping the same pipeline and rerunning most of the steps. So I believe the main issue here is still locks.

Hey!

One way to solve this is using contractual penalty - but this can go both ways. Meaning, the buyer might want contractual penalty for delayed handover. Also, the common practice is to limit the maximum amount of penalties - meaning, if the cap is reached, we will have to find another way. 0,5% per day might be limited to 10% of the agreement sum. If the vehicle costs 17 000 EUR, this means storing penalty is 85 EUR per day.

The other way is to solve this by using storage cost in accordance with the applicable Incoterms shipping clause - I presume it is FCA Bolt location? So, for example: FCA Tallinn, Osmusaare 3 (FCA, Incoterms 2010), by 21.02.2024. Should the delivery be delayed due to the fault of the Buyer, the Seller reserves a right to charge storage fee of 12 EUR/per car/per day. If the delivery for 24 cars is delayed for 3 weeks, we can charge them additional 24x21x12 = 6048 EUR.

NB! Delivery term sets how and when the delivery is made and who bears the risk.

Hi, 

Current set-up in WD for would need to be changed so that it matches the reality on how it is set up in Finland. Vacation year in Finland should be according to below: 

* 1st of April until 31st of March. 

How vacation should be accrued: 

* Employees receive 2 days of paid annual leave per month, adding up to 24 vacation days earned during the first year. In Finland the work week is between Monday-Saturday each week, which means this corresponds to 4 total weeks of vacation. Since the work week at Bolt is between Monday-Friday, we have set up an accrual of 1.67 vacation days per month in Workday.
* After your first year of employment, you start accruing vacation days corresponding to 5 weeks vacation in a year, which is 2.5 days per month and 30 days per year in the Finnish system of counting the work week from Monday-Saturday each week. Since the work week at Bolt is between Monday-Friday, we have set up an accrual of 2.08 vacation days per month in Workday.
* You cannot carry over vacation during your first year. 
* After your first year, you can carry over 5 days per year.

Following your inquiries, we have consulted with our legal team to address your concerns. Unfortunately, the specified clause cannot be amended, as it adheres to the legal framework outlined in Lithuanian law. Please find a detailed explanation below.

In the partnership model with Bolt, we function as a platform operator, facilitating a marketplace for retailers and consumers to engage in sales agreements. As Bolt is neither a party to the sales agreement nor the holder of the retail license for alcohol sales, legal obligations for compliance with alcohol selling requirements do not fall under our scope.

These activities include age verification and adherence to permitted hours for alcohol sales.

Based on the above, while the law does not impose direct liability on Bolt as a platform operator, our platform is configured to assist retailers in achieving the necessary compliance. We are continually working to enhance these measures.

Grouping by strategy query, after filtering out orders with destination changes.

{noformat}WITH order_try_dd AS (SELECT dd.lat AS dd_lat,
                             dd.lng AS dd_lng,
                             ot.driver_lat AS d_lat,
                             ot.driver_lng AS d_lng,
                             ord.destination_lat AS do_lat,
                             ord.destination_lng AS do_lng,
                             ot.created AS ot_created,
                             ot.search_token AS search_token,
                             ot.id AS ot_id,
                             ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
                             ord.id AS order_id,
                             ord.city_id AS city_id,
                             dd.created AS dd_created

                      FROM ng_public.dispatch_pref_driver_destination dd
                          JOIN ng_public.dispatch_pref_driver_destination_location ddl
                               ON ddl.driver_destination_id = dd.id AND ddl.driver_city_id = dd.driver_city_id
                          JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot
                               ON ot.driver_destination_location_id = ddl.id AND ot.driver_city_id = ddl.driver_city_id
                          JOIN ng_public.company_order ord
                               ON ord.id = ot.order_id AND ord.city_id = ot.city_id
                          LEFT JOIN (SELECT os.order_id, os.city_id
                                     FROM ng_public.company_order_stop os
                                     WHERE os.type = 'change_point'
                                       AND date(os.created_date) >= date('2023-11-10')
                                       AND date(os.created_date) < date('2023-11-29')) changes
                                    ON changes.order_id = ord.id AND changes.city_id = ord.city_id
                      WHERE date(ot.created_date) >= date('2023-11-10')
                        AND date(ot.created_date) < date('2023-11-29')
                        AND date(ord.created_date) >= date('2023-11-10')
                        AND date(ord.created_date) < date('2023-11-29')

                        AND dd.created < ot.created
                        AND changes.order_id IS NULL
                      )

SELECT COUNT(t.order_id),
       srd.strategy_name
--        ((dd_lng - d_lng) * (do_lng - d_lng) + (dd_lat - d_lat) * (do_lat - d_lat)) AS COSIN
FROM order_try_dd t
    JOIN glue.core.search_result sr
         ON sr.search_token = CAST(t.search_token AS BIGINT) AND sr.city_id = t.city_id
    JOIN glue.core.search_result_driver srd
         ON srd.search_log_id = CAST(sr.id AS VARCHAR) AND srd.driver_id = t.driver_id
WHERE ((dd_lng - d_lng) * (do_lng - d_lng) + (dd_lat - d_lat) * (do_lat - d_lat)) < 0
  AND sr.created_hour > date('2023-11-10')
  AND srd.created_date > date('2023-11-10')
GROUP BY strategy_name{noformat}

[~accountid:5b7d5435b57ed25933f64464] the consideration here is whether these surveys can be classified as competitive intelligence (which is legal) as opposed to industrial espionage (which is not). I am of the view that the survey questions are acceptable. However I think it must be emphasised that the survey questions are voluntary and participants are not obliged to answer any questions they do not feel comfortable answering. Consider including this wording, *“**_Your participation in this survey is entirely voluntary. If you feel uncomfortable or are unable to respond to certain questions due to confidentiality concerns, please skip those questions”_*

In addition I think where you ask “are you driving on Uber Black” and “what percentage of your trips come from Uber Black” you should consider inserting the option “not entitled to say”. 

You should also put a disclaimer that if they are bound by any confidentiality obligations then they must not complete the questions which would result in a breach in such confidentiality obligations. I suggest the following disclaimer, “*_If you are bound by any confidentiality obligations, contractual agreements, or legal commitments that would be breached by your participation in this survey, you are expressly prohibited from completing any questions that may result in such a breach.”_*

When you send the surveys perhaps you should include the following covering note, “*_This survey is designed to gather information for research purposes. Any information provided will be treated with the utmost confidentiality, and efforts will be made to aggregate data to protect the identity of individual respondents.”_* which will hopefully encourage participation and honest answers.

Had a call with Andrea in which we discussed the problem. There are two ways to approach this.

h3. 1. ETAs

We send the *SR Acceptance Screen* to drivers (and thus we send them to destination) based on the ETAs we receive from {{rides-routing}}. If drivers arrive too early, it means that ETAs are not precise.

Therefore we’d need a mechanism to “overwrite” the ETAs estimates.

*PROPOSAL*

introduce a configurable variable in admin (on a city level) that allows us to "delay" the  {{pickup_range_start}}

Example:

* we enable "delay pickup_range_start” feature in London
* we configure *pickup_start_range_delay* = 120 (2 min) 
* for London, when the check to display SR screen runs, instead of considering original range *[start; end]*, it considers *[start+2; end]*
* run tests on cities and see if the percentage of drivers arriving before_time_window decreased

PROS

* doesn’t interfere with ETAs results, just on cron logic of pickup interval. The only change would be to [this|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/c8fdb22a839457fb606f6e167632d928bc14b691/src/rides/marketplace/order/main/cron/service/scheduledRide/DriverBookingConfirmationService.ts#L178] part that can be rewritten as: 
{{const pickupIntervalStart = row.pickup_time + Math.min(row.pickup_interval, 0) + config.startRangeDelay;}}

CONS

* it’s kind of a “dirty hack”, motivated only by the results present in the CSVs

h3. 2. StartDriving button

The cause could be also that drivers click “StartDriving” button too soon. Solution would be to remove the “StartDriving” button and just rely on the *SR Acceptance Screen* logic (as it is, no changes needed on pickup range).

In order to validate this assumption, we should ask DATA team to enrich the previous CSVs with the percentage of drivers who tapped on the “StartDriving” button vs the one who arrived early because of the cron logic.
Comments are provided to the marketing in the document. Thanks a lot for your work with this.
for now we’ve decided to first ask DATA if the “StartDriving” button is the cause.

Hi [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] I’m sorry, this took me so long, but here is the answer. Hopefully this works 🙂 

The meaning behind the word “contract” is explained more throughly in the same Terms and Conditions section 4. 

In another words, confirming a journey with a driver leads to a separate agreement between the passenger and the driver. This means that the driver is acting as a service provider to whom the customer has accepted to pay for the received service. Communication of the terms of the contract are done through the Bolt online platform, including details like the pickup location, destination, fare, and any additional conditions. Other legal responsibilities are brought out in the Terms and Conditions. 

It's important to clarify that Bolt is a facilitator in connecting customers with drivers, but the direct contractual relationship is between the customer and the driver. Bolt acts as an intermediary and has its terms of service that users agree to, but it is not a party to the specific transportation contract.

Hello [~accountid:615d90da9cdb93007288f515] ,

As you already know, we are always defending de statement that couriers are self-employed workers.

In this sense, we act accordingly, differentiating ourselves in our approach from what could be considered an ‘employment relationship’; One of the main characteristics of an employment relationship is that workers are under the ‘control and supervision’ of the employer, and that is why we consider that blocks entail a certain risk of reclassification.

Regarding the blocks, the most risky would be the statistical one since it may be considered that, in this way, couriers are under our company’s direction.

On the other hand, regarding the example in question in which there can be a reasonable understanding that there has been inappropriate conduct on the part of the courier, as long as the measures taken in consequence are proportionate, it is reasonable to apply blocks in pursuit of the proper functioning of the platform and correct provision of service.

It is suggested that blocks be kept to a minimum, be reasonable, and, when applicable, follow the logic that certain behaviors beyond certain standards are not tolerated, in order to preserve quality and reputation, in the interest of all parties involved, whether couriers, partners, or the platform services provider.

In conclusion, if, according to your team's criteria, a behavior is deemed unacceptable and/or detrimental to the service, a block may be applied, although caution is recommended.

Please let me know if this overview is responding to your concerns.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

From a UK perspective, clawback provisions for immigration fees are very common. To avoid dispute, it is important that such agreements are very clear on what the specific items are that can be clawed back (as the attached template is). One important point to note, to the extent Bolt utilises the scheme, is that the costs relating to the Immigration Skills Charge can never be passed onto employees. If the Home Office become aware of any such arrangements, it is possible for them to revoke the sponsor licence.

In Malta it is not possible to agree on such amount deduction from the employees final salary contrary to UK (2.4. and 2.5. in UK template).

 In both jurisdictions, it possible to adjust the clawback mechanism in terms of amount (e.g., up to 100% of any fee incurred) and length (e.g., for repayment to be possible even after several years).

The Bolt entity should also be updated if needed.

Please note here, that the PO Year validation should also consider, that a Purchase Order may be raised from a prior year, than when the invoiced is processed. Let’s say a PO is raised on 10th December, and invoice is processed on 10th January. If the integration looks at sysdate, for year, then it will say this is invalid because it’s last year’s PO but this is actually accurate. So, that’s a case to consider here in the requirements. 

Here, I would also like to bring attention to *what* the integration is actually doing, based on the spare parts logic implemented in December 2022. 

Telema does not automatically *scan* invoice lines. This is a system limitation that has been identified. I am not talking about eInvoicing here, only PDF. Since the supplier invoices need to include all invoice lines stated, the logic that we have implemented is that PO lines are *copied* onto the invoices. Why am I stating this? Because this could have an impact on future-logic that we will need to review as part of procure-to-pay. Given that a valid PO is found, against the *Order* field in Telema, then it will copy it and add *one dummy prepayment line,* meaning that an accountant/AP goes into the invoice, applies whatever prepayment has been paid and submits that invoice - it then of course goes into 3-Way matching etc. There is the prepayment functionality coming in March 2024, hopefully. 🤞 

*My suggestion is the following:* 

# Build the formatting logic, and *only* apply it to EE003 only at this time. The *Order* number field in Telema, must therefore match the validation, as we have discussed in the meeting two days ago, and matching what Piret has sent. If the logic can be built for EE003, then in the future it can be replicated for other companies. I am considering three factors here: 
## limited time that Tim has to build, test and deploy this due to leaving 30th November.
## EE003 being currently the only company that has POs live *HOWEVER* once this logic is built, someone else from integration team can take this logic to apply to other companies as POs are being rolled-out. Integration Team time has been allocated to the P2P project accordingly, and overall Telema structure will need review and redesign, given that we are going to decrease dependancy on Telema coding (automation as part of P2P). 
## There are no Bolt Market invoices being processed from WMS against EE003 entity. This means that we have the room for flexibility, of only accepting Workday PO numbers into this entity. 
# For all other companies - pass the order field as External PO Value. 

I believe that this approach will be best for this time being, and goes in line with what Aida and Piret had suggested. 

We will for sure need to have another Telema review and potentially re-build next year, as we’re adapting the solution with our purchasing process. This will allow Aida to progress with the Bolt Market team for the 3-Way matching, and ensure that no errors occur in EE003 for the as-is live solution.

I will await the finance team’s approval whether we can proceed with this approach. I understand, in ideal world we would have this validation built for 45+ entities, however it’s something that time and resource permitting I do not think is achievable within 1 week time.

My suggestion is that we go as follows:

* If the company is EE003 (or others in the future), check if the PO# is a Workday PO using the validation rules provided by Piret and Witek.
** If the PO is correctly structured, check if it exists in Workday
*** If Yes, process.
*** If No, send error to Telema.
** If the PO is incorrectly structured (or isn’t a Workday PO)
*** Put PO number in External PO number field.
* If the company is any other company
** Put the PO number in the External PO number field.

What this means is that accountants have to be very careful checking that the “PO-<company>-##-” is correct in Telema before sending. That way, we can ensure that it is ‘correctly structured’ and send a relevant error message once it determines that that PO # doesn’t exist in Workday for any reason. This is also the way that we ensure all WMS invoices appear in the External PO field.

Considering Witek’s comment regarding WMS, and the amount of effort it would require for the Tech team to manage further indepth validation for WMS, I think this is the best possible option.

h2. Testing

To test this we need to complete the following test cases:

# *Supp Invoice with no PO number for EE003*
#* Invoice should appear in Workday without issue.
# *Supp Invoice with no PO number for <any>*
#* Invoice should appear in Workday without issue.
# *Supp Invoice with a valid Workday PO number for EE003*
#* Invoice should appear in Workday with 3-way matching and linked PO to Invoice
# *Supp Invoice with a non-existent but correctly structured Workday PO for EE003*
#* Invoice should error out and send “Non-existent PO” error to Telema.
# *Supp Invoice with a non-existent and incorrectly structured Workday PO for EE003*
#* Invoice should be entered with data in External PO field.
# *Supp Invoice with any other (for example, WMS) PO # for EE003.*
#* Invoice should be entered with data in External PO field.
# *Supp Invoice with a Workday PO number for <any>*
#* Invoice should be entered with data in External PO field.
# *Supp Invoice with a WMS PO number for <any>*
#* Invoice should be entered with data in External PO field.
# *Supp Invoice with a random string of words in the PO number field for <any>*
#* Invoice should be entered with data in External PO field.

* When there is a GSM call in progress an incoming in-app VoIP call can be accepted, but the GSM call has a priority on the microphone, so the Driver won’t hear the Rider.
* When there is an in-app VoIP call in progress an incoming GSM call can be accepted, but the GSM call has a priority on the microphone, so the Driver won’t hear the Rider.

{noformat}select 
	fdd.source as fdd_source,
	fdrl.country,
	count(*) as number_of_docs
from glue.ng_public.fleet_driver_registration_log fdrl
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.fleet_ocr_task_queue as fotq ON fotq.external_entity_id = fdrl.id
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.fleet_documents_document AS fdd ON fdd.id = fotq.document_id
where fdd.id is not null
and fdrl.country in ('ro', 'pl')
AND fdd.created > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '14' day
group by fdd.source, fdrl.country {noformat}

[https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04JRUL6FK2/p1700641207460339|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04JRUL6FK2/p1700641207460339|smart-link]

The row_number wrapper is to get the latest row for each document as some had multiple evaluations due to a bug (thx [~accountid:62976730563d380068b20459] for the query)

{noformat}SELECT
    *,
	100.0 * validDocsCount/(rulesFailureCount + validDocsCount) as ruleAcceptanceRatePercent
FROM (
    SELECT
        document_type,
        SUM(case when decision = 'passed' then 1 else 0 end) as validDocsCount,
        SUM(case when decision_reason like '%missing%' then 1 else 0 end) as veritasIssuesCount,
        SUM(case when decision_reason like '%invalid%' then 1 else 0 end) as rulesFailureCount,
        SUM(case when decision_reason like '%dependent_doc_verification_failed%' then 1 else 0 end) as dependantDocFailed,
        count(1) as total_documents
        FROM (
            SELECT
                fotq.document_id AS document_id,
                fotq.document_type,
                fdd.status,
                fotq.flow_run_uuid flow_run_uuid,
                daad.decision,
                daad.decision_reason,
                ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY fotq.document_id ORDER BY fotq.created DESC) AS rn
            FROM glue.ng_public.fleet_ocr_task_queue AS fotq
            LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.driver_auto_acceptance_document AS daad ON (daad.document_id = fotq.document_id)
            LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.fleet_documents_document AS fdd ON fdd.id = fotq.document_id
            WHERE fotq.external_entity_type = 'driver_registration'
            AND fotq.status IN ('failed', 'done')
            AND daad.decision IS NOT NULL
            AND fotq.created > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '14' DAY
        ) AS rn
    WHERE rn = 1
    GROUP BY document_type
);{noformat}

* Currently we approve only ~12% out of all uploaded documents, main root cause is WRONG_DOCUMENT_TYPE returned from Veritas. The false positives rate is low: *0.05%*. More details [here|https://bolt.enterprise.slack.com/docs/T02SA4XL8/F066NTW84JU].
* Excluding document with WRONG_DOCUMENT_TYPE we get on average *85.5%* rules acceptance rate. See individual rates per document type in the previous comment.

In order to increase the coverage we need the fix from Veritas regarding WRONG_DOCUMENT_TYPE issue. More details [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05B96H11LP/p1700061845185949].

* *[Quick "fix"]* Reset TTL prior to call to instrument service.

It might be possible due to a day-end ride,bonuses/compensations usually, the orders finished at midnight are added to the next day’s balance, as the balance calculation is based on the time stamp.

This causes a time difference between the payout system and the balance system. However, the balance and the payout is correct. It is only a discrepancy in the reporting. Most importantly they have received this difference in the next payout.

Please check the new [view balance|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/balance?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_date_ts%22%3A1696197600%2C%22end_date_ts%22%3A1696802400%2C%22types%22%3A%5B%22ride_hailing_fleet%22%5D%2C%22external_id%22%3A67889%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] to check the correctness of the payout.

And please check the [record|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/records?recordFilter=%7B%22action_timestamp_from%22%3A1696197600%2C%22action_timestamp_to%22%3A1696802400%2C%22from_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22from_agent_id%22%3A67889%2C%22agent_filter_operator%22%3A%22OR%22%2C%22to_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22to_agent_id%22%3A67889%7D&page=%7B%22limit%22%3A100%2C%22offset%22%3A0%7D] of the end days of Sunday (in this example will be a different timezone because of my location)

This is the cause of the day-end order, the record was created on 27.11 at 01:04 (your time will be 00:04)but the time stamp is for the previous day so that is why sometimes reflected in the reports ( as some report still pick data from admin v1)

!Screenshot 2023-11-27 at 13.44.38.png|width=1674,height=576!

As payout id done by created date recors, it wasn’t included but captured in the balance. This difference will be included in the next payout.

You have some very valid points and I absolutely agree that communication can always be improved. I’ll try to answer your additional questions as best as I can and just add some reasoning behind why we do things this way. This doesn’t mean that this won’t change and I have already shared your thoughts with the relevant parties. 

{color:#006644}Would it be possible for me to be permanently enlisted to the health insurance program - so that, unless I send notice asking otherwise, you would extend my health insurance for each subsequent year?{color}
Currently no, but it’s an option worth discussing for future periods. One of the problems with this, is that once your insurance starts you cannot opt out of it and change to Stebby until the insurance period runs out, so in case you actually wanted to try Stebby after your Confido insurance ended but you forgot to do so, then you wouldn’t be able to switch. However, we can help an employee switch if it’s the other way around and for example they forgot that they wanted to try Confido, we can still add them even if the insurance period already started. So right now it gives the employees more flexibility. 

{color:#006644}I bet there are a lot of people who lose their insurance because they did not read #all-estonia at the right time to know to send notice of their continued interest in health insurance. It is unreasonable to presume that people are always up to date with everything written on #all-estonia. Why this matters is that some employees may later come claiming their employer for damages - on grounds of the employer having made statements which lead the employee to believe that he/she was insured where in fact he/she was not and had to incur cost as a result. So this is an issue.{color}

police has answered:
Rechtliche Verpflichtung (Art. 6 Abs. 1 Buchst. c DSGVO) Gemäß Art. 6 Abs. 1 Buchst. c DSGVO darf ein Verantwortlicher Daten übermitteln, wenn er die Daten aufgrund einer rechtlichen Verpflichtung verarbeitet, der er unterliegt. Sofern die Polizei daher auf Grundlage der Strafprozessordnung (§§ 160, 161, 161a oder auch 163 StPO) als Ermittlungsperson der Staatsanwaltschaft oder in eigener Sache bei Gefahr in Verzug tätig wird, ist das Unternehmen grundsätzlich rechtlich verpflichtet, in den Grenzen der StPO Auskunft zu erteilen. Hier ist zu berücksichtigen, dass das Unternehmen – wird es z.B. als Zeuge gemäß §§ 48 ff. StPO herangezogen – ggf. keine Verpflichtung zur Aussage trifft, sondern dass die Auskunft gegenüber der Polizei auf freiwilliger Basis erfolgen kann oder Zeugnisverweigerungsrechte bestehen können. Überwiegende berechtigte Interessen (Art. 6 Abs. 1 Buchst. f DSGVO) Daneben lässt sich die Übermittlung auch über Art. 6 Abs. 1 Buchst. f DSGVO rechtfertigen. So erkennt der Gesetzgeber die Weitergabe von Daten im Rahmen der Strafverfolgung in Erwägungsgrund 50 der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung als berechtigtes Interesse des Verantwortlichen an: „Der Hinweis des Verantwortlichen auf mögliche Straftaten oder Bedrohungen der öffentlichen Sicherheit und die Übermittlung der maßgeblichen personenbezogenen Daten … an eine zuständige Behörde sollten als berechtigtes Interesse des Verantwortlichen gelten.“ Die schutzwürdigen Interessen des Betroffenen werden hier regelmäßig hinter den berechtigten Interessen des Verantwortlichen zurücktreten. Denn die Mitwirkung an der Aufklärung ist – wie oben beschrieben – eine gesetzliche Verpflichtung. Zudem besteht auch beim Betroffenen in der Regel ein Interesse, den Tathergang korrekt aufzuklären.

Hi Team,

Sharing the recommendation from the local counsel. 

Summary:

* Bolt may be liable for damage caused by a scooter caused "by the thing itself" in the Czech Republic as the owner of the thing that caused the damage (if you do not prove that the damage was caused by another person).
* Liability for damages can be discharged if you can prove that the item was properly supervised by you. The external counsel cannot guess what exactly this means in the case of supervision of a parked scooter - he sees a lot of room for judicial discretion here.
* The key in court will be proving the facts of the case, which will be difficult for Bolt here. The costs of the court proceedings may significantly exceed the amount you are currently being asked to pay.
* Unless we are able to provide evidence to prove another person caused the damage, Bolt is liable for the damage as the owner of the item. Bolt can only win the case if we can prove that we did not neglect to properly supervise the item (what exactly that means will be for the court to decide).

Detailed analysis:

The insurance company's claim is based on the application of § 2937, paragraph 1 of the Civil Code, which reads as follows: 

"_If a thing causes damage by the thing itself, the person who should have had supervision over the thing shall compensate for the damage; if such person cannot be otherwise determined, the owner of the thing shall be deemed to be the owner. Whoever proves that he did not neglect the proper supervision shall be exempt from the obligation to compensate_."

The application of this provision has its specifics, in particular:

* The injured party must prove that the injury occurred, that the injury was caused by the thing itself, the causal connection between these two prerequisites, and that the party causing injury breached his duty to supervise the thing.
* When the law says that damage occurs by the thing itself, it means that it has its origin in an internal cause (there is no immediate external stimulus).
* Every internal cause must be activated by something from outside. This trigger cannot be the direct action of man on the thing, because the provision does not protect against man's action. Therefore, a thing does not cause harm by itself if it occurs as a result of the direct (immediate) influence of a person who uses it for his activity and the harm is, for example, the result of faulty or unprofessional handling.
* The Civil Code identifies the person responsible for the damage in the first place as the person who should have had control over the thing. This can be anyone who has the thing in his possession by virtue of any title: a tenant, a borrower, or even without a legal reason (e.g. a thief or a vandal). Only secondarily, if such a person cannot be identified, the owner is the obliged person. If the owner manages to prove in his defence that someone else should have had supervision over the object, the hypothesis of the legal presumption is not fulfilled and the owner is not liable for compensation.
* If the person liable proves that he did not neglect to exercise proper supervision, he is released from the obligation to compensate for the damage. This possibility applies not only to the person who should have supervised the thing, but also to the owner, who becomes the liable party if it cannot be determined who should have supervised the thing.

The following conclusions are relevant to your particular case:

* It is crucial to prove the manner (mechanism) by which the damage was caused.  This will determine the legal classification of the case. The situation will vary depending on who caused the damage:
* Your user, e.g. by crashing an e-scooter into the damaged car. Then the user is liable.
* A random vandal who pushed the e-scooter and it fell on the damaged car. The vandal is then liable
* The e-scooter fell because of vibrations caused by a passing car, weather conditions, etc. Then Bolt is liable as the owner of the item.
* If it cannot be determined who caused the damage, then, Bolt is liable as the owner of the thing.
* Unless you can prove that another person caused the damage, the legal presumption that the owner of the scooter, Bolt, is liable for the damage applies. I don't know the facts of the case (I don't know the evidence presented to the court), so it is a question of whether you can prove another person was at fault. I suspect that you will be at a significant evidential disadvantage in court as to who caused the damage (you could prove it from CCTV footage for example, but after all the time you will find it hard to find it).
* Consider whether it makes economic sense to pursue this legal defence. It follows that you will be at a significant evidential disadvantage and risk losing the lawsuit. If you decide to litigate, your costs will be further increased, both for my legal representation and potentially for the costs you will have to pay to the insurance company if they are successful at trial.
* Liability can be avoided if you have exercised "proper supervision" over the scooter. The parameters of sufficiency in supervision are by no means set out to cover all possible cases in their uniqueness. The starting point must therefore be reasonable requirements for the proper and responsible handling of the supervised item, which are either derived from general practice and generally accepted rules, or, particularly for more complex equipment, may be standardised by certain standards (manuals) for professional handling.

The final summary is:

* You may be liable for damage caused by a scooter caused "by the thing itself" in the Czech Republic as the owner of the thing that caused the damage (if you do not prove that the damage was caused by another person).
* The key in court will be proving the facts of the case, which will be difficult for you.
* The costs of the court proceedings may significantly exceed the amount you are currently being asked to pay.
* Liability for damages can be discharged if you can prove that the item was properly supervised by you. I cannot guess what exactly this means in the case of supervision of a parked scooter. I see a lot of room for judicial discretion here.
* I also put the question of the responsible entity up for consideration. The lawsuit is against Bolt Services CZ, s.r.o. It is possible that another entity of the Bolt group is the owner of the scooter, which may have an impact on the outcome of the proceedings.The question is how much the court will deal with this fact, given that it is very difficult for the injured party to determine the ownership of the scooter (and therefore the responsible entity).

 Recommendation:

* Unless you are able to provide evidence to prove another person caused the damage, Bolt is liable for the damage as the owner of the item. You can only win the case if you can prove that you did not neglect to properly supervise the item (what exactly that means will be for the court to decide).

I would recommend that before going Live (after Testing), the Privacy Notice is updated to reflect a new purpose for GPS data. 

Considering that this is only a limited Test, and the fact that Ghana’s DSA only started enforcing their law on August 14, 2023, I believe the risk is low/medium.

*_Automated decision-making if you are a user of the rental services_*

*What personal data do we process?*

When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, i.e. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking and collisions.

*How do we process your personal data?*

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings:

#  *first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehaviour;
#  *second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and
#  *third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

Please be aware that we should not reissue any invoice upon request for reasons like: no NIP number at the time of issuance or it was incorrectly given and the rider/driver provided the number later, rider requests change of address or name later on.  It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoice for these reasons.

This type of fraud is actually exclusive to cash trips. AZ market has gotten to a stage where drivers have gained in-depth knowledge of how we operate through years of experimentation and they’re aware of our current procedures. They know that any type of in-app trip fraud will result in us doing a full refund and therefore don’t bother with in-app trips.

The target demographic for this type of fraud are tourists, specifically the ones that have just arrived at the airport. Since it’s their first time using Bolt and they’re in a new country, drivers target them as they are unaware and more susceptible to manipulation. After increasing the price in the app through fraudulent means, they demand more money from these tourists, claiming that it’s within their rights since that is the amount shown in the app. Even if tourists ask for help from other people, they have no way of proving that the price has increased and therefore almost always end up paying *10 times* the normal amount.
