Short conclusion would be that regardless of whether we apply this “promo code” functionality, *this topic is related mainly to unfair commercial practice and also very closely related to misleading advertising.* 

Therefore, the smaller the control group rate is, the better. Whether 10% is too big or not compared to 5% that we have today - probably more a question to business. But *considering the fact that compared to previous years the number of Bolt Food users has increased even more then I wouldn't´raise the control group rate to 10%* +*UNLESS*+ *we use the promo code functionality* +*AND*+ *other safeguards brought out above.*



*SAFEGUARDS*

However, regarding the +temporary+ rate increase (from 5% to 10%) +before the promo code functionality+ is launched, then I think it would be ok, if we raise the rate to +10% only for about 3 months+ or so IF we use *following safeguards:*

# *Complaints numbers.* We have seen that there haven´t been complaints/there have been only few complaints (to Bolt directly or to the authorities) regarding this practise so far. If the complaint rate rises OR is already high then:
## we shouldn´t raise the control group rate to 10%, *but* could consider raising it just a bit according to our needs, e.g to 7%, or  
## we should lower it back to 5% when the complaints number increase notably.  
# *Control group changes.* Ideally the control group should change every time with the new “test”/discount/promotion. Right now I understand we don´t change the control group for each new promotion/discount, we change the control group just after every 4 weeks. Would it be possible to change the control group for each new “test”/discount/promotion OR if the answer to this is no, then could we consider changing the control group more frequently, e.g. after every 2 weeks?
# *Communication period.* The communication period for certain product offers for certain individual is as short as possible.
# *Indemnification.* Person should get refunded or further explanations  +in case of complaint+ (e.g sth in the lines of: “we apologize for the technical error, see your offers now on app”)

*RISKS* 

*Consequences of practicing unfair commercial practice and/or misleading advertising (which may be the case right now):*

* when practicing unfair commercial practices at least here in *Estonia* it would be: punishable by a *fine of up to 400,000 euros.* {color:#ff5630}*NB!*{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}This may differ by country, i.e be higher, lower. Also there could be other sanctions in other countries. 
* violation of general requirements for advertising (i.e providing inaccurate information) at least here in *Estonia*  would be: punishable by a *fine of up to 10 000 euros.* {color:#ff5630}*NB!*{color} Again, this may differ by country,  i.e be higher, lower. Also there could be other sanctions in other countries. 

Whether these risks would be realized is always decided case by case. But considering the fact that Bolt is quite “visible” especially in the Baltic states therefore, being in a bigger spotlight for customers and also for authorities, then *I would be especially careful with increasing control group rates up to 10% in the Baltics*  +*without*+ *“promo code” functionality AND* +*other safeguard measures*+ *mentioned above.*



If you have any further questions, please let me know. Hope that this helps 🙂 

Liisa

[~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] (product counsel) and I are not convinced of the appropriateness of this blocking for the following reasons:

# We never know the reason why drivers don't respond to calls. It could be the case that the driver has a personal matter (being in the hospital, sick, attending a wedding, etc.) or that the driver has simply chosen to answer incoming calls from Bolt when he/she is not driving. Blocking a driver who has not answered a call because he is attending to personal matters seems disproportionate to me.
# Requiring drivers to always answer Bolt call and penalizing them for not answering our calls would be strange even if the driver were our employee, but it is even stranger when the driver is an independent contractor who can perform services whenever he wants. 
# In addition, we don't see how blocking the driver would solve this problem. Our expectation is that the driver will see that he is blocked once they return to the platform. We would not be able to get in contact with the driver until then.

Therefore, we advise against this but would be happy to discuss further if this will assist.

Many thanks.

wunschgemäß übermittle ich Ihnen hiermit die Rechtsgrundlagen für das gestellte, polizeiliche Auskunftsersuchen zum Zwecke der Strafverfolgung.

Rein vorsorglich weise ich darauf hin, dass Zeugen in einem Ermittlungsverfahren gemäß §§ 160ff. StPO verpflichtet sind gegenüber der Staatsanwaltschaft Auskünfte zur Sachverhaltsaufklärung zu erteilen. Strafprozeßordnung (StPO) § 160 Pflicht zur Sachverhaltsaufklärung (1) Sobald die Staatsanwaltschaft durch eine Anzeige oder auf anderem Wege von dem Verdacht einer Straftat Kenntnis erhält, hat sie zu ihrer Entschließung darüber, ob die öffentliche Klage zu erheben ist, den Sachverhalt zu erforschen. (2) Die Staatsanwaltschaft hat nicht nur die zur Belastung, sondern auch die zur Entlastung dienenden Umstände zu ermitteln und für die Erhebung der Beweise Sorge zu tragen, deren Verlust zu besorgen ist. (3) Die Ermittlungen der Staatsanwaltschaft sollen sich auch auf die Umstände erstrecken, die für die Bestimmung der Rechtsfolgen der Tat von Bedeutung sind. Dazu kann sie sich der Gerichtshilfe bedienen. (4) Eine Maßnahme ist unzulässig, soweit besondere bundesgesetzliche oder entsprechende landesgesetzliche Verwendungsregelungen entgegenstehen.

Die Polizei als ausführende Ermittlungsbehörde vertritt die Staatsanwaltschaft. Strafprozeßordnung (StPO) § 161 Allgemeine Ermittlungsbefugnis der Staatsanwaltschaft (1) Zu dem in § 160 Abs. 1 bis 3 bezeichneten Zweck ist die Staatsanwaltschaft befugt, von allen Behörden Auskunft zu verlangen und Ermittlungen jeder Art entweder selbst vorzunehmen oder durch die Behörden und Beamten des Polizeidienstes vornehmen zu lassen, soweit nicht andere gesetzliche Vorschriften ihre Befugnisse besonders regeln. Die Behörden und Beamten des Polizeidienstes sind verpflichtet, dem Ersuchen oder Auftrag der Staatsanwaltschaft zu genügen, und in diesem Falle befugt, von allen Behörden Auskunft zu verlangen. (2) Soweit in diesem Gesetz die Löschung personenbezogener Daten ausdrücklich angeordnet wird, ist § 58 Absatz 3 des Bundesdatenschutzgesetzes nicht anzuwenden. (3) Ist eine Maßnahme nach diesem Gesetz nur bei Verdacht bestimmter Straftaten zulässig, so dürfen die auf Grund einer entsprechenden Maßnahme nach anderen Gesetzen erlangten personenbezogenen Daten ohne Einwilligung der von der Maßnahme betroffenen Personen zu Beweiszwecken im Strafverfahren nur zur Aufklärung solcher Straftaten verwendet werden, zu deren Aufklärung eine solche Maßnahme nach diesem Gesetz hätte angeordnet werden dürfen. § 100e Absatz 6 Nummer 3 bleibt unberührt. (4) In oder aus einer Wohnung erlangte personenbezogene Daten aus einem Einsatz technischer Mittel zur Eigensicherung im Zuge nicht offener Ermittlungen auf polizeirechtlicher Grundlage dürfen unter Beachtung des Grundsatzes der Verhältnismäßigkeit zu Beweiszwecken nur verwendet werden (Artikel 13 Abs. 5 des Grundgesetzes), wenn das Amtsgericht (§ 162 Abs. 1), in dessen Bezirk die anordnende Stelle ihren Sitz hat, die Rechtmäßigkeit der Maßnahme festgestellt hat; bei Gefahr im Verzug ist die richterliche Entscheidung unverzüglich nachzuholen.

Eine zwangsläufig mit Unannehmlichkeiten verbundene Durchsuchung Ihrer Geschäftsräume sowie eine Zeugenvernehmung Ihrer Angestellten können Sie dadurch abwenden, dass Sie zu dem oben bezeichneten Beweisgegenstand eine schriftliche Auskunft erteilen und die dazu gehörenden Unterlagen, notfalls in originalgetreuen lesbaren Fotokopien übersenden. Auch die zwangsweise Vorführung ist zulässig (§§ 161a, 51, 70 StPO). Zur Vorlage der Beweisunterlagen besteht ebenfalls eine gesetzliche Verpflichtung, die notfalls zwangsweise durchgesetzt werden kann (§ 95 StPO).

Strafprozeßordnung (StPO) § 161a Vernehmung von Zeugen und Sachverständigen durch die Staatsanwaltschaft (1) Zeugen und Sachverständige sind verpflichtet, auf Ladung vor der Staatsanwaltschaft zu erscheinen und zur Sache auszusagen oder ihr Gutachten zu erstatten. (2) Bei unberechtigtem Ausbleiben oder unberechtigter Weigerung eines Zeugen oder Sachverständigen steht die Befugnis zu den in den §§ 51, 70 und 77 vorgesehenen Maßregeln der Staatsanwaltschaft zu. Gerichtliche Entscheidungen nach den Sätzen 1 und 2 sind unanfechtbar. (4) Ersucht eine Staatsanwaltschaft eine andere Staatsanwaltschaft um die Vernehmung eines Zeugen oder Sachverständigen, so stehen die Befugnisse nach Absatz 2 Satz 1 auch der ersuchten Staatsanwaltschaft zu. Created a potential fix in this [PR|https://github.com/bolteu/food-delivery-provider-app/pull/2727]. 

The fix would implies the following: it hides the order for 5 seconds or since the ETA is properly computed.
This aims to achieve the following behaviour:

* happy path: we receive an order with ETA stored in polling (i.e. “order_preparation_eta” is not null) → we show the order
* “order_preparation_eta” is null for 1 polling session path: we do not show the order for 5 seconds, until the next polling presents the ETA
* “order_preparation_eta” is null for more polling sessions path: we do not show the order for 5 seconds, and afterwards we show it without ETA



How to test?

# Activate the centralize flag 
# Create orders and notice that when an order is displayed, it will always have the ETA
# To make sure that such a case is replicated, watch the Charles logs and once we receive an “order_preparation_eta” = null, but the order was displayed alongside the ETA, then we have tested the behaviour
# Note that the <“order_preparation_eta” is null for more polling sessions path> is (should be :D ) highly unlikely to reproduce

criminal Procedure Code- Thailand



52- Section 52.- When a person is required to a appear before ail inquiry official, or a superior administrative. or police official, or a court in connection with an inquiry, preliminary examination, trial or any other matters in a accordance with the provisions of this Code, such person shall be served with a summons issued by the inquiry official or superior administrative or police official or the Court, as the case may be. However, in case of an inquiry official, or superior administrative or police official conducts the inquiry in person, such official shall have the power to require the attendance of the alleged offender or witness without serving a summons on such person.

132- Section 132.- For the purpose of collecting evidence, the inquiry official has the power as follows: (1) To· examine the person of the injured person with his consent or the person of the alleged offender, or any thing or place which may be used as evidence, including the ta~ of photographs, the drawing up of plans or sketches, the mouiJ~g or . ,. the taking of finger-prints, hand or foot-prints and the recording of any particulars likely to clarify the case;"In inspecting the body of a injured person or an alleged person according to the first paragraph, if such a injured person or lleged person is a female person, a female officer or other woman a . shall be an inspector, all this, in case where it thinks fit, the injured person or the alleged person can bring any person to be together in such inspection." (2) To search for articles the possession of which constitutes an offence, or which are obtained through an offence or used or suspected of having been used for the commission of an offence or which may be used as evidence, but the provisions of this Code governing search must be complied with; (3) To issue summons to a person who possesses any article which may be used as evidence, but the person so summoned needs not come in person and shall be deemed to have complied with the summons if the article as specified therein is produced; (4) To detain all the articles found or produced as provided in sub-Section (2) and (3) .



237- "Section 237.- The note of witness' testimony in the stage of preliminary examination or trial shall be read by the Court to the witness to listen in the present of the accused person except in case as provided in the section 165, the third paragraph. In case of parties' agreement, the Court may permit to take the testimony note in the stage of preliminary examination as a witness' testimony in the stage of trial and the witness has not to give a new testimony or the witness giving testimony can immediately answer the accused person's cross-examination, except accusation of statutory offence with minimum rate of imprisonment for five years up or more severe punishment."

* "Section 237 bis.- Before the entry of the charge in Court, when there are reasonable grounds to believe that the witness will depart from the Kingdom, has no habitual residence, or has residence far from the Court of trial, or there are reasonable grounds to believe that he will be tampered directly or indirectly, or there are other necessary causes which make _it difficult to bring him to give testimony in the future, the Public Prosecutor, himself or on the application of the injured person or the inquiry official, may apply by motion specifying all the acts alleged to have been committed by the alleged offender to the Court to give order granting that his testimony be taken promptly. It the alleged offender has been ascertained and kept in custody of the inquiry official or the Public Prosecutor, the Public Prosecutor shall bring him to the Court. If he has been kept in custody of the Court, the Court shall further call him for trial. When having received such application, the Court shall take the testimony of the witness promptly. The alleged offender may cross-examine or appoint a counsel to cross-examine the witness. In the case according to the second paragraph, if it is the case where the alleged offender is alleged to commit the criminal offence which if the criminal prosecution is instituted, the Court has to appoint a counsel for him or the accused has right to apply to the Court to appoint one for him according to Section 173, the Court shall ask the alleged offender whether he has a counsel or not before the. taking of the witness' testimony begins. In the case where the Court has to

 appoint a counsel for the alleged offender, if the Court is of opinion that it can appoint one for him in time, it shall do so and proceed with the taking of the witness' testimony promptly. But, if the Court is of opinion that it can not appoint a counsel for him in time, or the alleged offender can not appoint one in time, Jhe Court itself shall examine the witness for him. The memorandum of the witness' testimony shall be read out to him and if the alleged offender is in Court, the Court shall read it out before him. If the alleged offender is then charged to be the accused in the commission of the criminal offence, such testimony may be admitted in the trial of the case. In the case where an alleged offender is of opinion that if he has been charged as an accused, the person who is necessary to be adduced as his witness will depart from the Kingdom, has no habitual residence, or has residence far from the Court of trial, or there are reasonable grounds to believe that the witness will be tampered directly or indirectly, or there are other necessary causes which make it difficult to bring him to give testimony in the future, the alleged offender may apply by motion showing reasons and necessities to the Court to give order granting to take the witness' testimony promptly. When the Court thinks fit, it may give order granting to take the witness' testimony and it shall inform the inquiry official and the Public Prosecutor concerned. In the taking of the witness' testimony, the Public Prosecutor has right to cross-examine him, and the provisions of the third, forth and fifth paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis. The provision of 172 ter shall apply mutatis mutandis to the taking of the testimony of the witness who is a child not yet over eighteen years of age."

Additional comments from the external lawyers:

* Does the ‘Relocation Guide’ that is referred to also apply to employees in the UK, and does this set out what is being offered, maximum amount for things like flights or removal costs etc, and whether anything is specifically excluded (i.e. we would usually expect accommodation costs to be excluded)? If not, we would suggest that this is noted somewhere, either in the guide or in the expenses agreement in order to set expectations with the staff. The attached agreement makes clear that any expenses are at the company’s discretion and must be approved in advance in writing in any event but it will likely avoid questions from staff as to what is permitted.
* We note that the German agreement provided for tapering of the repayment amount by 1/12 for each month the employee remained employed after the effective date. We have not copied that wording as we understand from your email below that the business decision is for the recovery of up to 70%. However we would note that tapering of the sum would help ensure that it is not viewed as a penalty clause. In the attached draft we have stated that the employee must repay 70% or such lower amount as shall be communicated by the company, which provides some discretion but if you would prefer to also include the tapering arrangement similar to the German style you could do that.
* We have included wording which allows for the repayment sum to be deducted from sums due to the employee. We have also noted that in the event that the full amount can’t be recovered by a deduction, the employee will repay it as a debt within 3 months although we have left this timescale in square brackets and it can be updated to best suit the business.
* At clause 7 we have included square brackets around [is terminated / terminates] as this clause could either be triggered when notice is issued, or when the contract actually terminates. If it is triggered when notice is issued then that would be more favourable to the company especially given the ability to then deduct sums from payments due to the employee, although it being triggered when the contract actually terminates may be more in keeping with language used.
* We note from the other agreements that expenses can be approved by either the company or the Relocation Agency. We would generally not recommend delegating such authority to a third party but we have left this in at clause 5 if that is your normal practice and would suggest that it is made clear to the agency what their specific levels of authority are so that you retain control over this.

Hey guys, as Lise stated, this whole flow of rejecting campaign discounts on business orders wasn’t a decision made by Fraud. It was pushed to us by Business product and we just assisted in implementing using our fraud engine. The way that it’s structured, what happens is that we don’t apply discounts for [users|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C8YGKDSBG/p1701246364276769] who have already enjoyed discounts with another business company. So let’s say user A had a discount with company A1 before. If user is added to a company A2 that also has discounts, those discounts won’t be applied to this user specifically. However, the discount remains active on company A2 so other users of that company can still use it. The way we see it, it’s only a problem if the person who is getting their discount rejected is the only user of company A2. If that’s not the case, the company A2 still gets their discounts and it shouldn’t matter which users get them, what changes here compared to the previous flow is that it might take longer for them to get their full 50 discounted rides. Instead of literally their first 50 rides, will be their first 50 rides done by users that are not user A. However, if company A2 only has user A and user A already had a discount from another company, we have every right to reject them to get another discount. I do see the legit scenarios that might be caught in this logic, but again, this wasn’t our logic and decision. Business product discussed and proposed that themselves due to users that were creating multiple companies to abuse these signup discounts.

Why do we have github and npmjs proxies:

* *npm.internal* - required to reduce network traffic between builder machines (we install a lot of packages). It’s hosted in the same machine so it’s efficient & fast.
* *github package manager* - most of the UIP projects use this (and generally native, web projects), just because it’s managed and nice user interface
* *nexus* - should be the future of package managers, maybe we can get rid of npm.internal & github package manager. (GH has performance problems + moving packages between repos not possible)
* *reason for proxy* - bolt-server needs to consume {{@bolteu/*}}  scoped packages such as {{@bolteu/mqtt-client": "2.9.0",}} . @bolteu scope is attached to github repo, so npm.internal should have proxy to download the scoped packages correctly. While examining the marker rendering process, I discovered two interesting things:

1.
We have duplicates of dot images for markers (some examples [one|https://images.bolt.eu/store/2023/2023-02-23/4a086ecf-170d-443d-ad93-c6c782950c65.png], [two|https://images.bolt.eu/store/2022/2022-04-20/55aeb2b8-ddb7-4e2d-9078-b29db10140f3.png], [three|https://images.bolt.eu/store/2022/2022-04-20/55c1a1d3-9e79-4da3-ba24-90f71052e037.png]). The reason is that all these resources are uploaded manually by OPS team and we don’t have any checks for duplicates on backend (admin). 

The idea is to limit the choice of images for dots, or maybe even transfer the generation of dot images to the client side since such images are rather trivial.

2.
There are a bunch of models that differ only slightly from each other (see attached for examples). I understand that we have a fairly rich fleet of vehicles. Still, it seems that such detail on markers doesn’t provide any useful load for the user, but increases the consumption of memory and computational resources on the devices. 

The idea is to combine similar pictures somehow, leave only one, and use it for similar models. I think the most important thing is to reflect, for example, body variations (sedan, SUV, etc) and brands. All other small details like the color of the side mirrors, body kit options, etc. are not at all important.

[~accountid:712020:b2a2738f-c1f1-447c-9b72-29851b5fed3e] looped me in with this ticket for assessing antitrust (i.e competition law) related risks.

In this case that you have described here there indeed might be some antitrust related risks. Antitrust rules prohibit agreements between market operators that would restrict competition, and the abuse of dominance

*Why would antitrust related issues concern us?* - In cases when Bolt Food platform (“Bolt Food”) has a dominant position (market share ≥40%) in the market we should be especially careful if we want to share non-public and restricted information known only to Bolt Food with certain Bolt Food Partner(s) (Bolt Market is seen as Partner) which may give to certain Partner(s) (e.g. Bolt Market) an advantage compared to other Bolt Food Partners, since this type of information sharing may constitute as preferential treatment which may have negative effect on competition and therefore, may be seen as a form of abuse of dominant position by Bolt. 

*Fines for infringement of competition law can reach up to 10% of annual global turnover.*

*NB!* Since, according to European Commission's 21st of Nov [+press release+|https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_23_5944] European Commission is carrying out unannounced inspections at the premises of companies active in the online ordering and delivery of food, groceries and other consumer goods, then we should be especially mindful with projects where competition law related risks are highlighted (i.e. if possible, implement suggested “safeguards” as much as possible). 

+*Your team´s idea is doable from competition law perspective if following “safeguards” are considered:*+

# *Market share.* Make clear what is Bolt Food´s market share in the market where you want to target the Bolt Food users with offers regarding Bolt Market:
## 🟢 market share <40% (non-dominant) → antitrust risks are low, safeguard measures are recommended, but not obligatory,
## 🔴 market share ≥40% (dominant) → antitrust risks are high, safeguard measures should be taken into account. If it is not possible to apply all of them then at least measures in points 2.1; 2.2; 2.4 - 2.6 should be applied to mitigate the risks which may lead to fines, etc.

2. *🚦Safeguard measures* in case if targeting will be launched in a market where *Bolt Food´s market share is ≥40%:*

2.1. +*Information used is of general nature*+*.* Bolt Food users data that will be used for targeting them with Bolt Market promotions should be with general nature e.g: email address, fact whether they have purchased something from Bolt Market previously or not. Using more detailed information, such as AOV,  frequency of orders from other retailers, basket content from other retailers, etc., should be avoided.

2.2. +*Information used should not involve data about competitors*+*.* Using information about the competitors (e.g: from which competitor targeted user has purchased before; how many times targeted user has purchased groceries from the competitor; what was the content and/or value of the basket purchased from the competitor, fact that user abandoned other stores cart, etc.) should be avoided.

2.3. +*Offer the targeted personal discounts only once.*+ It is strongly recommended that personal discounts will be used only once or until first purchase from Bolt Market is made i.e no additional discounts (based on this restricted data Bolt Food shares only with Bolt Market)  will be followed after the first purchase.  As an illustration: Bolt Food in principle knows that a customer likes to eat certain sandwiches (consisting of certain bread, cheese and ham) very frequently. If these products are offered to the customer on a discount (at a lower price than e.g. Rimi) permanently / for a longer period of time then it creates strong incentives for the customers to order his/ her groceries from Bolt Market (and not e.g from Rimi). In this case discounts could have anticompetitive effects which couldn´t be mitigated by other measures. 

           2.3.1. If however, it is decided that Bolt Food will target users more than once with Bolt Market                                  related offers, then it is strongly recommended that there should be some longer period                                 between the initial offers and repetitive offers + other safeguard measures should be                       followed. 

2.4. +*Communication should be neutral and of generic nature*+*.* Communication displayed in discounts should be very neutral and not indicate in any way that we have gathered detailed or specific information (see points 2.1 and 2.2) about users purchasing habits and now we are targeting them based on that information. {color:#4c9aff}*PS!* {color}[~accountid:623ace32562ab90069f80d3b]{color:#4c9aff} the example that you brought out under this ticket on 29.11.23 is OK, since it is enough of general nature. {color}

2.5. +*Creating a “wall”.*+ It should be avoided making shared data available to employees that are responsible for the different stages of relevant decision-making in respect of Bolt Market.

2.6. +*Compliance with laws and Terms & Conditions.*+ Any use of information must be in strict compliance with applicable T&Cs and regulations (GDPR - Privacy). According to the Partners T&C it is allowed for Bolt Food to share preferential information with Bolt Market. ❗Please note that although sharing this type of data may be allowed according to the T&C´s it must be allowed also from privacy and competition law perspective - that this why it is recommended to follow other safeguards above.

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].
